rationale: This is largely a stripped-down variant of the archive's "Stable Accrual EBITDA Confirmation" — VOL(wcap/at,3) is mechanically close to the accrual-volatility leg already tested — and it drops the accrual-level component that most plausibly drove that result, while a 3-observation VOL is a very noisy stability proxy.

The recch sign convention is handled correctly and the narrowing from broad noncash-current-asset growth to collections is a defensible diagnosis of the prior alpha/t-stat divergence, though trending an already-differenced cash-flow item over only three years is double-differencing that will be dominated by noise.

The expected sign contradicts the natural accrual-channel direction the rest of this program relies on — rising payables (apalch > 0) is a *negative* working-capital accrual, which the accrual anomaly says predicts *higher* future returns — so the hypothesis is at odds with the mechanism it claims to extend.

Internally consistent (TS_RANK of NEG(dpc/at) genuinely peaks when depreciation is at a historical low) and a substantive re-specification rather than a cosmetic tweak of the prior version, but it closely echoes the published Beneish DEPI earnings-quality construct and low dpc/at is heavily confounded with the capex/asset-age cycle.

Signs are coherent and the "other/tax accrual" channel is a genuinely under-tested residual component relative to the receivable-inventory-payable constructions already in the archive, though txach and aoloch are sparsely populated and coverage is likely to fall below the already-thin ~0.08-0.10 baseline.

It is close to a rediscovery of the archive's "Pretax Profit Receivable Slippage" (and of the well-known sales-growth/Beneish-DSRI receivable-quality anomalies), and the MUL(GROWTH(sale), oiadp/sale) construction is non-monotone — negative margins times negative growth produce high scores — so the first leg does not compute the "profitable growth" the hypothesis describes.
